messages.subject: Re: Using data and time with dateRangeInput for selection from data table/dataframe
parts:
If that column is POSIXct, you can get the date by using as.Date(). For example, Sys.time() returns the current time as POSIXct, and you can convert to a Date with:
> as.Date(Sys.time())
[1] "2015-07-31"

-Winston

On Thu, Jul 30, 2015 at 3:12 PM, JD <po...@okstate.edu> wrote:

I have a data table (currently) that has a POSIXct column, "TIMESTAMP-TS", in the first column. I want Shiny to let users select the other data in the other columns from the table by the date and time. For example, the snippet I am about to share has hourly readings. 

         TIMESTAMP-TS RECORD-RN BattV_Min-Volts ETos-DegC Rso-DegC
1 2015-05-19 12:00:00      4099           12.34     0.097    3.436
2 2015-05-19 13:00:00      4100           12.36     0.047    3.520
3 2015-05-19 14:00:00      4101           12.35     0.042    3.385
4 2015-05-19 15:00:00      4102           12.35     0.023    3.053
5 2015-05-19 16:00:00      4103           12.35     0.053    2.543
6 2015-05-19 17:00:00      4104           12.34     0.015    1.897

In this example, I tried to us strptime to get just to the dates, thinking this would simplify things, but that doesn't work for obvious reasons I hadn't considered at first. Is there a way to get the dateRangeInput to include time? Something that won't require me to do more programming than already exists? I am not very good at programming. I am open to other work-arounds. Would I have to do something like a dateRangeInput combined somehow with a drop down for the time increments?

I have several other data collections that have a similar first column. Those other datasets have different timestamps in the first column, i.e. 5 minute readings and smaller.
